findings: S1 [blocking] Species artefacts choose the organism: base species lists carry an 'Arabidopsis thaliana' row in many runs (menaquinone here), and candidate search takes every listed species. Proposal: search only the species of the paper's grounded proteins / reaction states (or the most frequent), never a species no process uses.

S2 [blocking] PathBank 'Generated Pathway <n>' records (created 2026) are not curated and produced a nonsense step and all 4 mouse base merges. Proposal: exclude by name pattern (or by a curated / export flag once it is known what marks curated content).
S3 Reactome species without taxId (Arabidopsis) -> KeyError. Proposal: pass the species dbId when taxId is missing, or skip that species.

S4 Budget: one PathBank extract takes ~35-40 s; with 3 pathways PathBank uses the whole 120 s and Reactome / WikiPathways fail on lipid A and human. Proposal: a per-source share of the budget (e.g. 50/25/25) or fewer PathBank pathways.

S5 Wrong name join: a grounded incoming row joins a grounded base row by name/synonym when their ids share no namespace (Coproporphyrin III -> coproporphyrinogen III). Proposal: in convert (or payload), do not join two grounded rows on a name or synonym alone; require an agreeing id.

S6 The paper's non-currency 'Adenosine triphosphate' row (with synonym ATP) still receives database ATP through merge_extension's synonym rename, so it can act as a hop edge. In these 6 runs no hop-1 step was linked to the core only through it (via.py check: 0).
S7 PathBank names carry tabs and padding ('lipid A disaccharide \t', '\t Chlorophyllide '); strip them in pathbank.to_neutral.
S8 Disease copies of one pathway (Gaucher Disease PW127250 = Sphingolipid Metabolism PW000148) both enter; the name dedupe misses them. Proposal: dedupe candidates by the steps' content.
